request.spec:
A steward can assign a REVIEW claim to a user (an entry and a button on the claim;
REVIEW_ASSIGNED naming the claim and ending user=<user>; a blank user, any other status or anyone
else is refused). The claim shows the assigned user, and the header shows the signed-in user the
count of REVIEW claims assigned to them.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can assign a REVIEW claim to a user (an entry and a button on the claim;
REVIEW_ASSIGNED naming the claim and ending user=<user>; a blank user, any other status or anyone
else is refused). The claim shows the assigned user, and the header shows the signed-in user the
count of REVIEW claims assigned to them.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Review assignment is in place and the main "review assignment" test passes under `bin/e2e`. The other three tests fail, and the failures don't appear to be caused by this change. Two look like problems in the spec, which I wasn't allowed to edit.

**What I changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V117__claim_review_assigned.sql`, adds a `review_assigned` column to the claim table. `Claim` has the matching field.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /claims/{id}/assign-review`, calls `ClaimService.assignReview`.
  - It refuses anyone who isn't a steward, a blank user, and any claim that isn't in REVIEW. A refusal writes nothing.
  - Otherwise it records `REVIEW_ASSIGNED … person=… amount=… date=… user=<user>`. The existing delegation handling adds `for=<steward>` when a delegate does it.
  - The claim's data now includes `reviewAssigned`. It stays on the claim after the review moves it to OPEN, which the test expects.
- **Front end:**
  - Each claim row shows `claim-review-assigned`, and has a `claim-review-user` entry and a `claim-review-assign` button. Refusals show in the row's `claim-error`.
  - The header shows `my-reviews-count`: the number of REVIEW claims assigned to the signed-in user.

**Test results**
- With `bin/e2e`, "review assignment" passes and scenarios 1, 2 and 3 fail.
- All three fail on a line expecting `sheet-parent` to read the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"`. That looks like a placeholder that was never filled in; it should be the test's own sheet id plus `-p`, which is what the app shows.
- I ran a temporary copy of the spec with that line fixed (since deleted). Scenarios 2 and 3 then pass.
- Scenario 1 then fails at line 321, expecting `claim-late-entry` to be "no" where the app shows "yes". The scenario soft-closes period 2026-04 and then adds a claim due 2026-04-06. The existing late-entry rule (`ClaimService.java:177-181`) marks such a claim late. That's an older feature this request doesn't mention, so I didn't change it. If this test is meant to pass, someone needs to decide which behaviour is right: the existing rule or the spec.

**Port conflict:** another process is now listening on port 3000. `bin/e2e` uses port 3000 by default, so it will fail to start the app until that process is stopped or `PORT` is set to another port. My last check ran on port 3917.
